title: HTML Checker Online: Find Errors Crawlers Trip On
description: Free online HTML checker: validate any URL with the W3C Nu engine and see the errors that matter for SEO first — head tags, nesting, duplicate IDs.
answer: An online HTML checker validates a page against the HTML standard and lists the errors. Enter a URL: we run it through the W3C Nu validator and put the errors that affect how crawlers read the page first — invalid elements in the head, broken nesting, duplicate IDs — ahead of the cosmetic ones.

trust: Validation is done by the W3C Nu HTML Checker, the same engine behind validator.w3.org. We sort its findings by SEO impact.
body:
## Does valid HTML matter for SEO? Mostly no — with one important exception. Google says it tries to understand HTML even when it's invalid, so a page full of minor errors can rank fine. The exception is the head: [if Google meets an invalid element in the head](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/valid-page-metadata), it ignores everything after it. faqs.q: Is HTML validation a ranking factor?
faqs.a: No. Google tries to understand invalid HTML, and validity itself is not a ranking signal. Errors matter only when they stop Google from reading metadata, especially inside the head.

faqs.q: Why does the validator report so many errors?
faqs.a: Modern sites include frameworks, third-party scripts and attributes that strict validation flags. Most are harmless. Focus on the errors we mark as SEO-relevant.

faqs.q: Can I validate a page behind a login?
faqs.a: No. We fetch public URLs only. For private pages, copy the HTML from your browser and paste it into validator.w3.org/nu directly.
